admission_primary.disagreement_rule: a module whose two columns disagree in SIGN is NOT admitted on the strength of either; the disagreement is itself the finding and is reported with the per-type table that produced it
admission_primary.recommendation: the OFFICIAL SLU-F1 stays the primary for admitting a slot module; the normalized SLU-F1 is the SECONDARY and must AGREE IN SIGN
admission_primary.why_normalized_is_reported_beside_it: the official metric charges a full word distance of 1.0 for a pure case or spacing difference, so a module can look effective by repairing spelling and a module aimed at RECALL can look weaker than it is. The normalized column separates the two: a gain that survives it is a gain in what was heard, and a gain that vanishes under it was a gain in how it was written
admission_primary.why_official_is_primary: it is the dataset's standard scorer at a pinned commit, it is the number every published SLURP line is stated in, and every verdict and lock in this repository already stands on it. A study that moved its primary to a metric of its own making after seeing the gap would be choosing the metric that flatters it

contacts.note: the only subprocess is the pinned official SLURP evaluate.py, which is the scorer and not a model; every token figure is the stated whitespace x 1.3 proxy and no tokenizer was called

normalized.note: the 3 unparsed rows carry 10 gold mentions and the normalizer never touches a row that did not parse, so this rung is a pure RECALL channel and its gain does not depend on the metric's spelling tolerance
